question.text: A Direct Broker in insurance differs from an Insurance Agent primarily because:

answer.text: A Direct Broker represents the insurer while an Insurance Agent represents the client
A Direct Broker can only sell life insurance products
A Direct Broker represents the client and can charge both fee and commission, while an Insurance Agent represents the insurer and gets only commission
A Direct Broker is limited to online sales only

explanation.text: The Logic: Pages 35-37 state that brokers represent the client, direct brokers can charge both a fee and earn commission, and insurance agents represent the insurance company and receive commission. The distinction is in who each intermediary represents and how they are remunerated. The Trap: Option A reverses the representation — it is the broker who represents the client and the agent who represents the insurer. Note: The page 35-37 framing is limited to the representation and fee/commission distinction; broader product-comparison or depth-of-knowledge claims are not stated on those pages.
